stem: Which statement about the three states of matter is correct?
subject: Science

options.rationale: Incorrect. Gases do have mass, even though it is small and they are often invisible.

options.text: A liquid takes the shape of its container but has a fixed volume.
options.rationale: Correct. A liquid flows to take the shape of its container while its volume stays fixed.

options.text: A solid changes its volume to fill its container.
options.rationale: Incorrect. A solid keeps a fixed shape and volume; it does not expand to fill a container.
options.misconception: A solid can change its volume to fit a container.

options.text: A liquid has its own fixed shape.
options.rationale: Incorrect. A liquid has no fixed shape; it takes the shape of its container.
options.misconception: A liquid has a fixed shape.

stem: A bar magnet is brought near several objects. Which statement is correct?
subject: Science

options.text: The magnet attracts all metals, including aluminium.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Magnets attract only magnetic materials (iron, steel); aluminium is not attracted.

options.text: A bigger magnet is always stronger than a smaller magnet.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Strength depends on the magnet, not merely its size; a small magnet can be stronger.
options.misconception: A larger magnet is always stronger than a smaller one.

options.text: The magnet can exert a push or a pull on magnetic materials.
options.rationale: Correct. A magnet exerts a push (repulsion) or a pull (attraction) on magnetic materials.

options.text: Two north poles placed together will attract each other.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Like poles repel; only unlike poles attract.

stem: In a circuit with a battery, wires and a bulb, the bulb does not light up. Which is the most likely reason?
subject: Science

options.text: The circuit is open at one point.
options.rationale: Correct. A break (open) anywhere in the circuit stops the current, so the bulb will not light.

options.text: Current is used up by the bulb so none returns to the battery.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Current is not used up; the same current flows through the whole series circuit.
options.misconception: Electric current is used up by the bulb so less returns to the battery.

options.text: The bulb can only light in an open circuit.
options.rationale: Incorrect. A bulb lights only in a closed circuit, not an open one.
options.misconception: A bulb lights up even in an open circuit.

options.text: Plastic wires conduct the electricity away.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Plastic is an insulator; it does not conduct electricity away.
options.misconception: Plastic is a good conductor of electricity.
